rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; MVP/MAYO-VDB), uses basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is more directly interpretable for PRS strength than the other candidates’ mostly full-model AUROC/C-index values. Main limitation: it is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, so strength relative to genome-wide shrinkage scores remains uncertain. Runners-up: PGS003972 and PGS003973 are from a coherent, disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with the same AAA endpoint and PRS-CS genome-wide construction; however, their reported discrimination is primarily full-model (AUROC 0.69; C-index 0.882) with unclear PRS-only contribution and unknown/limited covariate transparency (PGS003972 covariates unknown; PGS003973 uses age/sex only), so they are supportive but not decisively better than the OR-supported PGS000753. Framework-style portability models (PGS001784; PGS002054) are deprioritized because their evidence is more benchmark/framework-derived and their PRS-comparable metrics are modest (R2 ~0.014–0.015), while PGS003429 appears to be screening cost-effectiveness packaging with unknown covariates and only full-model AUROC (0.708), which is not a substitute for PRS-only performance.

All 4 candidates are direct-match for the target concept (alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder), but none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; performance evidence is therefore limited and not fully comparable. PGS002738 is best supported because it has the closest mapped concept alignment to the target (trait_efo="alcohol dependence"; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder") and provides a relatively strong, interpretable effect size metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a sizable EUR evaluation sample (n=7,900), with disease-focused multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). Runner-up PGS000201 has good endpoint fidelity via phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder (DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed)" and reports a larger incremental ΔR² vs covariates (0.01192) than its sibling PGS000202, but it is mapped to a measurement EFO rather than the disease EFO. Second runner-up PGS002739 remains a direct AUD model and reports OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76 (1.32–2.34), but its evaluation is AFR-only (African American or Afro-Caribbean), making it less broadly supported in this context than the EUR-evaluated options. Overall confidence is moderate because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) and covariate details are missing/uneven across candidates (notably unknown covariates for PGS002738/PGS002739).
